distinguishing_features: Passive helical strakes on a stationary centrifuge shroud suppress coherent vortex shedding rather than changing operating speed or monitoring component health.
The intervention targets fluid-structure excitation of a rotating bowl as a direct means of reducing resonant weld fatigue.
No new sensors, VFD waveform, motor-current inference, or temperature-based prediction is required.
parsed.objective_technical_problem: Reduce operating-speed resonant vibration and fatigue cracking of centrifuge-bowl welds by suppressing the external fluid excitation that sustains the resonance.
parsed.viable_reason: As written, the solution assumes without evidence that coherent vortex shedding drives the bowl resonance, while the 500 Hz estimate is not tied to operating or critical speed and the prescribed 5D strake height is implausibly large for the stated gap.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: Applying helical strakes to suppress vortex shedding is a routine flow-induced-vibration mitigation technique, so the distinguishing mechanism would be an obvious option to a skilled engineer once fluid excitation was identified.
